# Annual Review - 2023

## Professional Growth

### Achievements
- Led 3 major projects (authentication refactor, mobile API, analytics dashboard)
- Mentored 2 junior engineers
- Spoke at 1 conference (PyCon Norway)

### Lessons Learned
- Scope creep is the enemy - learned to say no earlier
- Documentation pays off exponentially
- Automated testing catches 90% of bugs before production

### Areas for Improvement
- Need to delegate more
- Should contribute to open source
- Better work-life boundaries

## Personal Projects

### Completed
- Smart home automation (presence detection)
- Personal finance tracker
- This annual review template

### Abandoned
- Mobile app for habit tracking (too much competition)
- Blog about machine learning (didn't enjoy writing)

### In Progress
- Mnemosyne (personal knowledge management)
- Learning piano (Grade 2 exam in March)

## Reading

Books read: 24 (goal was 20)

Best books:
1. Thinking, Fast and Slow - Kahneman
2. A Philosophy of Software Design - Ousterhout
3. The Pragmatic Programmer - Hunt & Thomas

Should read more fiction. Got too focused on technical/productivity books.

## Health & Fitness

- Running: 450km total (down from 600km in 2022)
- Gym: 2x per week (consistent)
- Sleep: Average 7.2 hours (target: 8)

Injury in June disrupted running routine. Need to be more careful about warm-ups.

## Relationships

- More intentional about keeping in touch with friends
- Weekly calls with parents
- Better at actually responding to messages

## Financial

- Emergency fund: ✅ 6 months expenses
- Investments: Up 12% (market was good)
- Big purchase: New laptop (necessary for work)

## 2024 Goals

1. **Professional**: Get promoted to senior level
2. **Projects**: Launch Mnemosyne beta
3. **Learning**: Complete machine learning course
4. **Health**: Run a half marathon
5. **Reading**: 25 books, at least 10 fiction

## Reflections

2023 was a solid year. No major surprises, steady progress on most fronts.

Key insight: Small consistent improvements compound over time. The daily notes habit I started in January has created a valuable archive of thoughts and ideas.

Looking forward to 2024 with cautious optimism.
